86	### 2.2 What a stop-loss honestly is here
87	
88	Four things, kept apart on the card, three of them named differently from today:
89	
90	| Card section | What it is | Who owns it | How it is computed |
91	|---|---|---|---|
92	| **What takes you out** | The events over-represented in the worlds where the stop was touched **first** | computed | `lift(k) = P(k happened before the stop ∣ stop first) / P(k happened)`, Wilson interval on the numerator, suppressed below 200 draws, with the median days between *k* and the stop |
93	| **What to watch** | The claim whose adverse flip hurts the terminal most, **and** resolves before it, **and** is publicly observable | computed | two-directional `sensitivity()` + INV-14's two filters. *Renamed from "invalidation"; it is a watchlist, not a stop.* |
94	| **Your risk exit** | The stop price, the target, the horizon | **the user types them** | never derived |
95	| **Execution** | — | — | We say one sentence: *a stop order's trigger is not its fill price*, and nothing else. |
96	
97	**The smallest thing that is both honest and impressive is "what takes you out".** Forty lines over a boolean mask; the brief's most distinctive sentence answered by computation rather than prose; the one output nobody in the competitive landscape ships. "What to watch" is fifteen lines and is the honest remnant of INV-14. Everything above them — expected shortfall, ruin, drawdown — is cut.
98	
99	**What each needs from the engine.** Only one thing, and it is small:
100	
101	```python
102	# katalyst/thesis/draws.py — the ONLY coupling between the finance layer and the engine
103	class Draws(BaseModel):
104	    day_zero: date; days: int
105	    order: tuple[PropositionId, ...]
106	    when:   NDArray[int]      # (n, claims): the day each claim first became true, −1 for never
107	    weight: NDArray[float]    # (n,): all ones for an exact ancestral sampler
108	```
109	
110	"What to watch" needs **endpoint marginals only** — today's `sensitivity()` gives them. P(stop first) / P(target first) need **event times per world**. The inverse query needs **joint samples with times**. All three come from `when`.
111	
112	`weight` is in the shape from day one so the finance layer is **indifferent to ENGINE's Plan A versus Plan B**: an exact core with an ancestral sampler gives weights of one, a likelihood-weighted sampler gives real weights, and nothing above changes. And `when` is derivable from *today's* engine too — `_draw` already computes `truth[claim] = came_true`, a `(versions, worlds, days)` boolean array, whose first true day **is** `when`. **So stack 05 is not blocked on the engine reformulation**: write it against synthetic `Draws`, test it against synthetic `Draws`, turn it on over whichever engine lands.

296	- **I did not run the frontend, Playwright, `make eval`, or anything that calls a model or costs money**, per the common brief.
297	- **I did not re-run the strike-branch numbers myself** (`apply` is not exported from `domain/branch.py` under that name and I stopped rather than hunt). I relied on `spec/multiverse/propagation.md:456`, which records the engine's own `.46 → .41` and `.43 → .36`.
298	- **I did not measure** how long a 20 000-draw daily path simulation takes over the Hormuz map. I estimate milliseconds in numpy over a `(20000, 45)` float array, but I did not run it. If it is slow, the draw count is the knob.
299	- **I did not verify** that the engine's `truth` array is still shaped `(versions, worlds, days)` end-to-end under every branch — I read `propagation.py:1444-1463` and confirmed the assignment, not the full lifetime.
300	- **I did not read** audit-G (generation) or audit-H (UX) in full, only their finance-adjacent rows; ENGINE, GENERATION and UX analysts cover those.
301	- **I did not price** the browser work beyond a line estimate; audit-H's dock placement is assumed correct without my checking the Inspector's section stack myself.
302	- **Calibration is untested and stays untested.** Nothing in this design validates that the model's probabilities are any good. The card says so; that is all it can honestly do.

## 2. The design I recommend

### 2.1 The rule that makes the comparison honest

> **A model number may be differenced against a market quote only when both range over the same set of worlds — so the edge is computed from the world with *no supposition in force*, and a supposed world can only ever show a conditional payoff.**

The smallest shape that enforces it is a **signature, not a guard**. The edge is never computed from "a world"; it is computed by one function that requires the base world as its own argument:

```python
# katalyst/thesis/edge.py — outside domain/, because it touches a quote (INV-11, ADR-0003)

class Quote(BaseModel):                     # what a venue says. Never merged with a model number.
    venue: str; contract_id: str
    p: float                                # the mid, as a probability
    spread: float                           # best offer minus best bid
    as_of: date; url: str
    source: Literal["fetched", "recorded", "user"]

class Edge(BaseModel):                      # built by `priced()` and nowhere else
    model: Belief                           # unconditional, owner='model'
    quote: Quote
    costs: float                            # half the spread plus fees, as a probability
    edge: float                             # model.p − quote.p − costs. Signed. May be negative.
    break_even: float                       # quote.p + costs — useful even with no quote
    mixture: tuple[MixtureTerm, ...]        # every term shown: P(H)·P(c|do H) + (1−P(H))·P(c|do ¬H)

class NotComparable(BaseModel):
    reason: Literal["conditional_world", "no_quote", "no_contract", "different_question"]
    said: str                               # the plain sentence the card prints
    break_even: float | None                # still printable when only the quote is missing

def priced(base: World, shown: World, claim: PropositionId, quote: Quote | None) -> Edge | NotComparable: ...
```

`base` and `shown` are two required arguments; there is no way to hand `priced` a branch world alone, and `Edge` has no other construction path. Tests: *agree with the market ⇒ edge reads exactly 0*; *a branch world alone does not type-check*; *a missing quote yields `NotComparable` that still prints the break-even.*

The **mixture** is the piece both reviews wanted and neither costed: after *Suppose Hormuz opens*, the card still says *"your supposition makes M1 .61; weighted by the map's own P(H) = .36 against the no-open world's .40, the unconditional number is .47 — that is the one compared with .48."* review/'s worked example, with the engine supplying the terms. It needs only `do(¬A)`, which exists.

### 2.2 What a stop-loss honestly is here

Four things, kept apart on the card, three of them named differently from today:

| Card section | What it is | Who owns it | How it is computed |
|---|---|---|---|
| **What takes you out** | The events over-represented in the worlds where the stop was touched **first** | computed | `lift(k) = P(k happened before the stop ∣ stop first) / P(k happened)`, Wilson interval on the numerator, suppressed below 200 draws, with the median days between *k* and the stop |
| **What to watch** | The claim whose adverse flip hurts the terminal most, **and** resolves before it, **and** is publicly observable | computed | two-directional `sensitivity()` + INV-14's two filters. *Renamed from "invalidation"; it is a watchlist, not a stop.* |
| **Your risk exit** | The stop price, the target, the horizon | **the user types them** | never derived |
| **Execution** | — | — | We say one sentence: *a stop order's trigger is not its fill price*, and nothing else. |

**The smallest thing that is both honest and impressive is "what takes you out".** Forty lines over a boolean mask; the brief's most distinctive sentence answered by computation rather than prose; the one output nobody in the competitive landscape ships. "What to watch" is fifteen lines and is the honest remnant of INV-14. Everything above them — expected shortfall, ruin, drawdown — is cut.

**What each needs from the engine.** Only one thing, and it is small:

```python
# katalyst/thesis/draws.py — the ONLY coupling between the finance layer and the engine
class Draws(BaseModel):
    day_zero: date; days: int
    order: tuple[PropositionId, ...]
    when:   NDArray[int]      # (n, claims): the day each claim first became true, −1 for never
    weight: NDArray[float]    # (n,): all ones for an exact ancestral sampler
```

"What to watch" needs **endpoint marginals only** — today's `sensitivity()` gives them. P(stop first) / P(target first) need **event times per world**. The inverse query needs **joint samples with times**. All three come from `when`.

`weight` is in the shape from day one so the finance layer is **indifferent to ENGINE's Plan A versus Plan B**: an exact core with an ancestral sampler gives weights of one, a likelihood-weighted sampler gives real weights, and nothing above changes. And `when` is derivable from *today's* engine too — `_draw` already computes `truth[claim] = came_true`, a `(versions, worlds, days)` boolean array, whose first true day **is** `when`. **So stack 05 is not blocked on the engine reformulation**: write it against synthetic `Draws`, test it against synthetic `Draws`, turn it on over whichever engine lands.

| Question | review/ | review2 | Who is right |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A price-valued terminal node** | Not needed; a scenario payoff table suffices | Blocker; add a fifth `kind` | **review/ is closer, and I go further: cut it.** A Position holds spot, vol and horizon honestly — the model cannot elicit them anyway. review2's own cost estimate (~120 lines) omits the new validity rule, the prompt change and the paid re-recording. |
| **Daily price paths** | "Defer daily dynamics" (`00:30`, `00:134`) | Build them; the time model earns its keep here | **review2, decisively — and review/ contradicts itself.** Its own §"Stop loss is path-dependent" says *"the tool should therefore show a coarse price path."* B6 asks for stop-losses; a stop is path-dependent; ~80 lines. |
| **Expected shortfall / CVaR** | Cut until a defensible P&L distribution exists | Cuts FR-24's suite in §5.2, then lists *"the 5% expected shortfall"* in §2.3 | **review/. review2 contradicts itself.** ES needs a capital base and reads as theatre. Cut. |
| **Two-sided payoff** | Scenario rows with both adverse and favourable legs | A scenario-conditional move distribution | **Neither, as a schema change.** The loss leg is the stop, which lives on the Position; the edge is already signed. Both reviews' *substance* — EV must be able to say *don't* — is met without touching the schema. |
| **Sizing** | Defer automatic sizing; a user-entered loss budget is enough | Risk budget primary, quartered Kelly as a ceiling at the band's bad end | **Both, reconciled.** We show what the user's own risk budget implies and a greyed Kelly ceiling labelled *never size to this*. Nothing is automatic; nothing is recommended. |
| **The nested band** | Remove it | Keep it as ~200 exact solves | **ENGINE's call.** Noted here because the Kelly ceiling is shrunk by the band's width, so *some* band must survive — `range_shares` already computes the machinery. |
| **Market data** | FRED is an observation, not a belief; recorded snapshots until live adapters exist | Polymarket keyless mid; user-entered first, ship in 05 | **Both, combined.** review/ is right about FRED; review2 is right that the user-entered path ships first and is forty lines. |
| **What "priced in" costs** | A design risk to fix before implementation | A blocker with ~60 lines of fix | **review2 on the size, review/ on the urgency.** It is cheap *and* it must be settled before the first line of 05. |

Where they **agree**, and both are right: the conditional-versus-unconditional trap (independently found, which is the strongest signal in either document); invalidation ≠ stop-loss; path products must go; the fixture's numbers contradict its prose; there is no position for a shock to hurt; and a conditional thesis with an honest *"no positive edge at this price"* is a complete result, not a failure.

Net effect: −60 lines in stack 04, +30 in stack 05, and the browser follow-up (`frontend/src/graph/diff/noChange.ts`) becomes a deletion instead of an addition. **This one needs Kent, because FR-11 is P0 and names the path product by hand.** |
| `feat/04b-evals` items 1, 2, 4, 5 | **Keep as planned.** | One addition to the eval rubric, at no structural cost: *does a `market` ending name an instrument that resolves on a real venue or ticker list?* The only real recording produced 11 price payoffs, 0 contracts, and 3 `market_without_payoff` rejections — nothing checks that any of those 11 instruments exists. |

---

## 5. Decisions that are genuinely Kent's

**D1 — Does `move` get a range, and does it ride with the payoff-`kind` fix?**
Today a price ending says *"short XLE against SPY, three per cent"* — one number with no range, while every belief on the map carries the range the model stated (decision record 0015). Two recorded answers for the same ticker gave `0.35` and `0.15`.
*On screen:* the card reads *"short XLE vs SPY, 6% (4–9%)"* instead of *"3%"*, and the P&L distribution widens honestly.
*In code:* `PricePayoff.move: float` becomes a small frozen `Move(mid, lo, hi)` in `domain/proposition.py`, plus one sentence in the prompt.
- **Recommended: add it to `fix/04-payoff-kind-required` now.** That branch already moves the prompt fingerprint, so the Hormuz recording must be remade either way. **Marginal cost: $0 and about 40 lines**, plus one session's delay to that branch. Risk: the model already omits payoffs (3 of 23 proposals in the one real recording were rejected for `market_without_payoff`); a nested range may push that rate up.
- Alternative: leave `move` a point and put the range on the Position form as a **user** number, labelled. Cost: $0, ~10 lines, and one more place where a model number renders as a confident point.
- Worst: add it in stack 05. Cost: **a second paid re-recording** (~$4 and 36 minutes for Hormuz, more if the other three are approved). Do not choose this.

**D2 — Drop the path product from `domain/` (`feat/04b-evals` item 3)?**
Both reviews say a path product along a route is not a probability of anything when claims share causes. FR-11 (P0) names it by hand.
*On screen:* the Verify verdict stops reading *"the multiplied-out likelihood is .07"* and starts reading *"opening moves this ending by 32 points, from a base rate of 40%"*, with the weakest edge named by ablation.
- **Recommended: drop it; write total effect in stack 05 instead.** Cost: −60 lines in 04, +30 in 05, and a browser deletion. Amends FR-11.
- Alternative: land item 3 as planned and delete it in stack 05. Cost: 60 lines written and then thrown away, plus a P0 requirement that was true for a week.

**D3 — Does M1 name a Polymarket contract that actually exists?**
The fixture's `contract_id` is an honestly-labelled stand-in (*"brent-below-70-2026-10-31"*). The demo's climax is *"the model says .46, the venue says .48."*
*On screen:* the contract title becomes clickable and opens the real market.
- **Recommended: spend half an hour searching Polymarket by hand for a live oil or Brent contract, and rewrite M1's claim, `contract_id` and `title` to name it exactly.** Cost: ~30 minutes plus one recorded JSON file. This is the highest value per minute anywhere in stack 05: it turns the fixture's single biggest honesty weakness into the demo's strongest moment.
- Alternative: keep the stand-in, mark the quote `source: "user"`, and say on the card *"illustrative contract; no venue quotes this claim."* Cost: nothing, and a reader who checks finds nothing at the other end of the link.

**D4 — Stack 05 without a docs-only chapters pull request?**
The roadmap's pattern is chapters first, then code. `spec/thesis/` is five promised chapters and a landing page. A stack is capped at four pull requests, and stack 05 needs all four for code.
- **Recommended: no chapters PR.** One short `spec/thesis/` chapter after PR 3, generated from the docstrings, or nothing. Cost: reverses ADR-0011's working rule (review2 proposes the same freeze for different reasons). Buys: the Thesis dock, which is the difference between a computed answer and a demo.
- Alternative: five chapters first, and the dock slips to stack 06.

**D5 — Is the derived thing a stop-loss, or a watchlist?**
`spec/thesis/README.md:7` says *"That is the stop-loss, and it is derived, not guessed"*, and PRD anti-pattern 11 says *"do not type the stop-loss by hand."* I verified the derivation yields nothing usable on the demo's own fixture: for M1, the only claim resolving before it is B — the thing the thesis is betting on.
*On screen:* the card grows a section called **What to watch** (computed, filtered, with dates) and a separate line **Your stop** which the user types, plus **What takes you out** (computed by lift).
- **Recommended: amend INV-14 and FR-23 to say *watchlist*, and let the user own the stop.** Cost: ~0 lines of code; an ADR and three document edits. Buys: the one claim in the product a risk quant would call indefensible, removed.
- Alternative: keep the wording. Cost: nothing to build and a question nobody can answer in the demo.

---

## 6. What I did not check

- **I made no network call.** I do not know whether a Polymarket contract matching M1 exists today — hence D3. The recorded-quote design is deliberately robust to it not existing, but the demo's headline is not.
- **I did not run the frontend, Playwright, `make eval`, or anything that calls a model or costs money**, per the common brief.
- **I did not re-run the strike-branch numbers myself** (`apply` is not exported from `domain/branch.py` under that name and I stopped rather than hunt). I relied on `spec/multiverse/propagation.md:456`, which records the engine's own `.46 → .41` and `.43 → .36`.
- **I did not measure** how long a 20 000-draw daily path simulation takes over the Hormuz map. I estimate milliseconds in numpy over a `(20000, 45)` float array, but I did not run it. If it is slow, the draw count is the knob.
- **I did not verify** that the engine's `truth` array is still shaped `(versions, worlds, days)` end-to-end under every branch — I read `propagation.py:1444-1463` and confirmed the assignment, not the full lifetime.
- **I did not read** audit-G (generation) or audit-H (UX) in full, only their finance-adjacent rows; ENGINE, GENERATION and UX analysts cover those.
- **I did not price** the browser work beyond a line estimate; audit-H's dock placement is assumed correct without my checking the Inspector's section stack myself.
- **Calibration is untested and stays untested.** Nothing in this design validates that the model's probabilities are any good. The card says so; that is all it can honestly do.

1	# Design after the midpoint reviews — what changes, what stays, and why
2	
3	**2026-09-21 · coordinator's synthesis, revised after one adversarial pass · KENT ANSWERED every question it raised the same evening (`notes/2026-09-21-decisions-after-review.md`, R1–R17).** Where this page says *proposed* or offers options, read the decisions note for what he chose: **events and states (R2); the path product replaced (R3); the spread lands with a disagreeing row greyed, not dropped (R4); one freeze after the flip, then all four examples recorded once (R5, R9); one plain probability per arrow (R6); `36%`, with the formatter moved to the browser first (R17 — this overturns §2.5's "formatting stays in `domain/`").** The decision records themselves are still written `proposed` and accepted by him before code is built against them. The plan that executes it is `PLAN.md`. The questions that are genuinely Kent's are in `notes/2026-09-21-decisions-after-review.md`.
4	
5	**Where it comes from.** Two independent reviews (`review/`, `review2/`) were digested by four read-only Opus analysts, each re-checking every finding against today's code (`main` = `48eb562`): `analysis/2026-09-21-digest-{engine,finance,generation,craft}.md`. A fifth agent then attacked the first draft of this page: `analysis/2026-09-21-red-team.md`. **Those five reports hold the evidence** — file and line, measurements — and their scripts are kept in `analysis/scripts/`. This page holds the conclusions, and says where an analyst was overruled. Kent's four answers to `review2` (2026-09-21) are treated as direction: **an exact core with a sampler on top · keep the time model and make it sound · land what is open, then finance before more generation · revisit generation.**
6	
7	**The bar** (Kent, 2026-09-21): rewrites of merged work are allowed *"but should be weighed against a high standard of quality improvement … the best tradeoffs in terms of work required versus improvements made."* And: the spec stays a first-class book; shorten it *where warranted*, not as a maxim.
8	
9	**How sure this page is.** §2 rests on prototypes of a few hundred lines on maps of five claims or fewer, not on the product. It therefore ends in a **spike with a kill criterion**, not a commitment. §3 is design on open ground. §4 rests on measurements of one real recording and three kept runs. §5 was judged from code and five screenshots, not from a running browser.
10	
11	---
12	
13	## 1. The verdict in six lines
14	
15	1. **The foundations stand.** Branches as patches, the validator that rejects and never repairs, locality, the typed wire, replay, the canvas and its keyboard: both reviews, four analysts and the red team say keep them. Nothing here is a rewrite of the product.
16	2. **The arithmetic does not.** Three defects reproduce on today's `main`, on the demo map, under 100% coverage. The band has an independent cross-check; **the likelihoods have none, and nothing independent runs under an edit** — that gap let all three through.
17	3. **The cure is a change of question, not a bigger sampler:** a claim's number becomes *the chance it happens by its deadline*; *whether* is solved exactly; *when* is sampled forward. It is right for *Suppose* to four decimal places. It is **not yet right for *This happened*** — the first draft of this page said "exact" there and the red team measured .12 of error. The engine stack opens with a spike that settles that before anything is built on it.
18	4. **The brief ends in a trade and the trade has no code.** Stack 06 builds it in four pull requests behind one narrow contract with the engine.
19	5. **Every change to what we ask the model for lands once, after the engine is proven**, then Hormuz is recorded once. The payoff `kind` fix waits for that.
20	6. **Less is built, on purpose** — §7.
21	
22	---
23	
24	## 2. The engine — what a number means, and how it is worked out
25	
26	### 2.1 The three defects (all on `main` today; re-run by the coordinator, an analyst and the red team)
27	
28	| | What happens | Root cause |
29	|---|---|---|
30	| **An observation never reaches a cause.** | Two claims, A → B. *This happened* on B leaves A at `.3000`; the right answer is `.4562`. It prints the same number as *Suppose this is true*. | The engine keeps each claim's worked-out likelihood and throws away the coin flip. For a claim with no causes that likelihood is the same in every world, so filtering worlds by the observation cannot move it (`propagation.py:1470`). |
31	| **Endings are deaf to half their causes.** | On Hormuz, supposing the insurance premium (C) or OPEC+ restraint (R) moves Brent (B) by .06–.17 and moves both endings by `0.0000`. | A trigger arrow reads its source on the day the source's **earliest** incoming arrow lands. For B that is day 2; C's push lands on day 7 and R's on day 5 — inside B's own series, invisible to B's outgoing arrows (`propagation.py:806-843`, `:1463`). |
32	| **A claim nobody believes deletes a supposition.** | Insert a claim with a prior of `.001` and an arrow of `−0.01` into a supposed claim: the tile never reads *Supposed*, on any day. | A supposition ends on a calendar worked out from the map's shape. It never asks whether the opposing cause happened, or how hard it pushes (`propagation.py:888-948`). |
33	
34	Also true: the range under an observation can be made entirely of coin flips (`.157` wide with every input frozen); and a merged test (`test_an_observation_moves_a_cause_even_when_no_arrow_pushes`) enshrines sampling noise as required behaviour.
35	
36	**A repair inside today's engine was costed and rejected** (engine analyst §3a): fixing the first defect there destroys the range or multiplies latency by thirty; fixing the second makes the settled day random, which the grid, the day-states, retraction and the locality proof are all built on. It *is* the reformulation.
37	
38	### 2.2 The design — proposed record 0016
39	
40	**A claim's number is the chance it resolves YES by its own deadline.** That is what the sentence on the tile already says. It is not a snapshot read on one day, and an event that has happened never un-happens.
41	
42	**The time model stays on the arrow.** `strength`, `lag`, `shape`, `half_life` keep their meanings. They now bend a *rate* — how likely the claim is to happen on each day — rather than a likelihood read on one day; the claim's number is that rate added up over its window. An impulse's whole area counts, so the answer no longer depends on where a deadline falls against a half-life (record 0014's admitted wart goes — the red team tried to break this with short impulses near a deadline and got gaps of `.0000–.0001`).
43	
44	**When a cause arrives comes from one forward pass, not from inference** — causes first, each claim's chance of having happened by each of 12–24 points in its window; a *Suppose* pins its claim to its day and the pass is redone. A child's yes/no table is its rate averaged over when its causes arrived. **Whether each claim happens is then solved exactly** by the standard method for a sparse network of yes/no claims (variable elimination: multiply the small tables together and sum out one claim at a time, cheapest first). The versions ride along as an array axis, so a whole range is one pass. *(Today there are 2 000 versions × 8 worlds. With exact answers there is no inner noise to average away; the analyst proposes about 200 versions. That is a new parameter, to be measured, not a description of today.)*
45	
46	**Measured** (scripts in `analysis/scripts/engine/` and `analysis/scripts/redteam/`):
47	
48	| | |
49	|---|---|
50	| `review2`'s own plan — exact over event *times*, 12 points, 20 claims with up to 3 causes | **0.7–7.8 s** per range, up to 63 million table entries; 58–119 s at 30 claims. Its own kill criterion fires |
51	| this design — exact over *truths*, timing from the forward pass | **0.5 ms**; 1.7 ms at 30 claims *(the red team did not re-run the timing)* |
52	| accuracy, **no edit**, against exact-over-times (560 numbers, adversarial four-claim maps, all three shapes) | mean `.00027`, worst `.0175`, 0.9% off by more than `.005` |
53	| accuracy, ***Suppose*** (4 480 numbers) | mean `.00007`, worst `.0259`, **0.2%** off by more than `.005` |
54	| accuracy, ***This happened*** (4 480 numbers) | mean `.00127`, worst **`.204`**, **6.6%** off by more than `.005` — the second figure the screen prints |
55	
56	**So "exact" is true of *Suppose* and not of *This happened*, and this page must not claim otherwise.** Evidence moves *when* a cause happened as well as *whether* ("if Brent fell, the strait more likely opened early"); the tables were built from timing before the evidence and never learn. It bites when evidence reaches a claim by two routes through impulse arrows; a plain chain is exact. The obvious patch — rebuild the tables from after-evidence timing — double-counts and is worse.
57	
58	**The spike that opens stack 05 settles it, with a kill criterion, before any product code.** Three candidates for *This happened*, each measured against the red team's exact-over-times enumerator on its adversarial maps:
59	
60	- **(a) Weighted forward sample.** Draw worlds forward *with times* — the sampler the trade needs anyway (§3) — and weight each by how well it matches the evidence. It integrates over *when* correctly, so it converges on the right answer; its cost is sampling noise on observation branches only. **This is Kent's own answer read literally: an exact core, with a sampler on top.** Recommended going in.
61	- **(b) Accept the prior-timing tables** and print an observation's numbers to the tolerance measured.
62	- **(c) Re-cut the yes/no variable per evidence day.** Larger tables; may be exact; may be slow.
63	
64	**Kill criterion:** if no candidate holds `.005` on 99% of the adversarial set inside 300 ms on a 20-claim map, the design is not adopted as it stands and Kent is told with the numbers.
65	
66	**Two oracles, two tolerances, proving two different things** (the first draft had one, and it could not have caught the error above):
67	
68	1. `test_the_elimination_is_exact` — `1e-9`. A brute-force sum over the core's **own** tables. Proves the elimination, the *Suppose* surgery and the conditioning arithmetic.
69	2. `test_the_tables_agree_with_integrating_over_time` — tolerance **measured in the spike and written in the record**. An enumerator forbidden the core's tables, built from the arrow's parameters alone, over the full joint of event times for maps of four claims or fewer; *Suppose* **and** *This happened*; must include an impulse and a diamond, because a step-shaped chain does not reproduce the defect. The red team's `rt_core.exact_over_times` is a working 80-line version.
70	
71	### 2.3 What the new meaning forces — three consequences the first draft hid
72	
73	**`sustain` does not survive on its own (red team M3, proved).** Today a `sustain` arrow differs from a `trigger` only because a claim can *un-resolve* when an impulse fades — which is precisely the defect §2.2 removes. Once "happened" is permanent the two are identical to six decimal places, and `mode` is dead data. Record 0005 calls trigger/sustain *"the best idea in the brainstorm"*, and Kent's direction was to keep it. So this is **his decision, and it is not optional** — one of:
74	
75	- **(i) Events and states** (proposed record 0017). A claim is an `event` (permanent once it happens) or a `state` (holds over an interval, and can stop). A `sustain` arrow may only leave a state. A state needs two times — on and off — and its tile sentence must say which question its number answers (*"holds on its deadline"*). Automatic retraction is **deleted**: *"Hormuz opens, then Iran is struck"* leaves both events standing, and the strike lowers the state *the strait stays open*, which is the claim everything downstream actually depends on. The brief's own sentence comes out right. Cost: the largest option; the model must say which kind each claim is, so **`persistence` must be in the one shape freeze**.
76	- **(ii) Events only; a sustained push is two arrows** — one from the event that starts it, an inhibitor from the event that ends it. Reproduces `sustain` exactly, costs one validity rule and one prompt sentence, adds no field. `mode` leaves the vocabulary. The cheapest sound option; it gives up a word Kent liked.
77	- **(iii) Keep today's snapshot meaning for states only.** Not recommended: two meanings of a number on one map.
78	
79	The third defect (a claim nobody believes voiding a supposition) dies under (i) and (ii) alike, because both delete retraction-by-calendar.
80	
81	**`World.series` changes meaning (red team M4, proved).** Today it is a per-day snapshot that is allowed to fall — the golden test pins `1.0 → .36 → .36 → <.10`. "The chance it has happened by day *t*" can only rise. So: an event's series is a rising curve; a state's series (under option i) is a snapshot that can fall; `DeltaRow.peak_delta` and `at_day` — whose rationale is "shows up for a fortnight and then unwinds" — apply to states and need restating for events. The first draft listed `series` under "kept untouched". It is not.
82	
83	**A supposed claim's stored `p = 1.0` has three readers, not one** (`diff.py:817`, `:460`, `apiSource.ts:263`), and `Belief.p` forbids a gap — so it stays.
84	
85	### 2.4 Honest cost
86	
87	The first draft said "3 sessions, net −350 lines", scoped to `propagation.py` alone. **Five to seven sessions is the floor, before the event/state decision**; nine or ten with option (i). What it forgot: `diff.py` (611 executable lines — `versions_of`, the version weights, the band import, `moved_only_by_reweighting`, `sensitivity`'s use of retractions, the ranked list's reading of `series`); the browser (two readers of `moved_only_by_reweighting`; the retraction badge, whose height is baked into the tile's geometry; the provenance sentence that prints "8 worlds under each"); **34 of `test_propagation.py`'s 46 tests**; the locality oracle, which must be rewritten and should get *stricter*; and about 400 numeric literals across `propagation.md` and `diff.md`. The comparable is #38, which fixed one defect class, kept every wire meaning, and cost 1 335 insertions across 12 files.
88	
89	**Staged so `main` is never red and the canvas never shows nonsense:** the two oracles, failing cases marked strictly expected-to-fail → the new core beside the old behind a flag, default unchanged → one flip that changes every number once, with the generated numbers file's diff as the complete statement of which → *then, separately,* the Verify door's replacement, and the event/state work. Four risks, four pull requests; the first draft bundled them.
90	
91	### 2.5 Riding with it
92	
93	- **The path product goes (rewrites INV-8 and FR-11 — Kent's).** Multiplying likelihoods along a route is not the chance of anything when claims share causes (if Y always equals X and both are .5, the product says .25 and the truth is .5). It was never moved into `domain/`; that item is dropped. `Verdict.product` becoming always-empty is a server-only change — the browser hard-codes the absence today. Replacement, once the core exists, each one or two extra solves: the **shift** the hypothesis makes to the destination; **the chance every step on the route goes right**, as a true joint; **which single arrow carries most of the shift**. The trade needs the first anyway.
94	- **The provenance spread lands now.** It draws one strength per arrow per *version*, and versions are the part of today's engine the new core keeps. Its visible effect on the scripted strike — two ranked rows instead of three; B and N1 read `unchanged`, N1 because its one arrow is the map's one bare assertion and 88 versions in 100 agree on its direction — is the product telling the truth, and the new `unchanged_because: versions_disagree` says so in words. **Kent sees it at M4.**
95	- **Formatting stays in `domain/`** — one analyst wanted it moved to the browser (a session); the engine analyst and the red team measured it at about twenty executable lines, tested against its browser twin. Fix the three places that print a raw float into text a reader sees. Revisit only if Kent chooses `36%` over `.36`.
96	- **Do not split `propagation.py`** — about 800 lines of code under long docstrings, and §2.2 rewrites most of it.
97	
98	---
99	
100	## 3. The trade — stack 06, on open ground
101	
102	Full design: `analysis/2026-09-21-digest-finance.md` §2. The load-bearing choices:
103	
104	**Like with like (proposed record 0018).** A model number may be set against a market quote only when both range over the same worlds. So an edge is computed from the world with **no supposition in force**, and the shape enforces it — one function, `priced(base, shown, claim, quote) -> Edge | NotComparable`, with no signature that takes a branch world alone. After *Suppose Hormuz opens* the card still reaches an honest number by showing the mixture term by term: *P(H) × the supposed reading + (1 − P(H)) × the reading with H supposed false*. With no quote it prints a **break-even** anyway — the most useful thing to say when there is nothing to compare.
105	
106	**A stop is a price the reader owns (proposed record 0019; amends INV-14, FR-22, FR-23, FR-24 and reverses PRD anti-pattern 11, *"do not type the stop-loss by hand"*).** The roadmap's derived stop-loss yields nothing usable on its own fixture — the only claim resolving before the Brent ending is the thing the thesis bets on — and the sweep only ever flips claims one way. Four things kept apart on the card: **what takes you out** (computed: which events are over-represented in the worlds where the stop is touched first); **what to watch** (computed: the adverse flip that hurts most, resolves earlier, and can be observed — the honest remnant of INV-14); **your exit** (stop, target, horizon — typed by the reader, never derived); **execution** (one sentence: a stop's trigger is not its fill).
107	
108	**One contract with the engine:**
109	
110	```python
111	class Draws(BaseModel):            # thesis/draws.py — the ONLY coupling to the engine
112	    day_zero: date; days: int
113	    order: tuple[PropositionId, ...]
114	    when:   NDArray[int]           # (n, claims): the day each claim first came true, −1 for never
115	    weight: NDArray[float]         # (n,): how much each world counts
116	```
117	
118	It lets stack 06 be written and tested against synthetic draws. **It is not a free decoupling** (red team S2): the thing that produces `when` is the forward sampler §2.2 introduces, and under an observation its times are only as good as the spike's answer. If candidate (a) wins, the same weighted sample serves both — one sampler, two readers. The stop-versus-target number is what a reader trades on, so the record must say which distribution the times came from.
119	
120	**One demo, one map** (red team S7). The walk opens the *recorded* Hormuz map, whose eleven trades all name a *price*, none a venue *contract*; the curated fixture has the one contract. So stack 06 makes a price ending first-class — a position, a first-touch answer, a break-even, and *"no contract quotes this claim — edge not calculable"* — and the edge-against-a-quote moment appears where a real contract is named. Whether the Brent ending should name a real Polymarket contract needs a look at the venue; it is on Kent's list.
121	
122	**Not built:** a fifth, price-valued kind of claim (a position already holds spot, volatility and horizon, none of which a model can supply — and the new kind would cost a validity rule, a prompt change and a paid re-recording); two-sided payoffs (the loss leg *is* the stop); expected shortfall, drawdown, ruin, portfolio risk, automatic sizing; Kalshi; an event-study helper.
123	
124	**Outside data with no key (proposed record 0020; amends 0010).** Quotes are recorded first and fetched second: a committed dated file the demo and the build run on; an opt-in live Polymarket read that falls back to it; a reader-entered quote always available. A FRED figure is a measured level — a spot anchor with its attribution line — never a `market` belief. On screen a quote is never a bare number: `Polymarket · .48 · recorded 2026-09-21`.
125	
126	**The export** is `legs[] + conditions[]`, never an order format, and carries its own limits **as data** (`refuses: [...]`, `not_advice`), so an agent that ingests it ingests the caveats. There is no "not investment advice" line anywhere in the repository today.
127	
128	**The fixture contradicts itself today:** the prose says model `.61` against market `.48`, "13 points of edge"; the engine says `.456`, so the flagship trade is a *sell* by accident, in six files (one of which corrects itself fourteen lines later). Its fixes belong to **whoever owns `fixtures/hormuz.py` at the time — the engine lane, at the flip** — not to stack 06, so two stacks never edit one file.
129	
130	**On screen** (craft analyst §2): no new real estate. One pinned three-line **YOUR TRADE** strip above the panel's scroll — the only pinned thing in the product; *what takes you out* and *what carries it* are the existing change-list component run on a different question; the outcome strip draws on the tradeable tile, which is why unselected tiles first collapse their two empty belief columns to a glyph row; the card is a state of the panel, never a dialog.
131	
132	---
133	
134	## 4. Generation — settle the shapes once, after the engine is proven
135	
136	Measured on the committed recording and three kept runs (generation analyst §0) — several of `review2`'s claims are out of date:
137	
138	- **The map is not a tree.** 1.12–1.37 arrows per claim, claims with two and four causes, `LinkProposal` used in 2 of 20 and 7 of 28 accepted proposals. The *quality* case for drafting a whole map in one call is gone; its remaining case is speed, and `review2`'s "3 minutes, $0.70" is, against the measured price and pace of a call, roughly 2× optimistic on time and 3× on money.
139	- **Search is the clock.** A call that searches takes 3–4× the seconds. 93 searches bought five base rates on eighteen claims; three of the five are `0/2`, `2/3`, `1/1`.
140	- **The recorded map has no arrow that pushes down.** The answer shape *allows* one (the `strength` field's description says so) and one kept run drew three; but the standing text never asks *what would stop this step*, and the scripted insert — which is adversarial — drew three negative arrows at once. The cheap fix is a question, not a shape.
141	- **`review2`'s evidence check cannot be built** — the search tool returns encrypted content and the structured answer carries no citations. `review/`'s version can: a quoted passage and the role it plays.
142	
143	**One shape freeze, then one paid re-record of Hormuz — and the freeze comes AFTER the engine's flip, not before it** (the first draft had it before; the red team showed three fingerprint moves would then have landed after the paid run — red team M6). Everything that changes the standing prompt or the answer shapes moves the prompt fingerprint and makes the recording stale, so it all goes together, once the engine has proven what it needs to be told:
144	
145	- **One number per arrow, not a free-floating strength — and it must mean one thing** (red team M7). The claim's own number is restated as what the code has always used it as: *the chance it happens by its deadline if none of the causes on this map happens*. Each arrow carries `p_if_only_this_cause`: *the chance the effect happens by that same deadline if this cause happens on the first day of the window and no other cause on the map does.* Our code derives the arrow's weight. Removed: the elicited `strength`, and with it "+1 triples the odds" — a number we wrote inside a prompt.
146	- `persistence: event | state` on a claim — **if** Kent takes option (i) of §2.3.
147	- `quote` and `role` on a source (`mechanism · magnitude · timing · resolution · instrument`); `what_would_change_my_mind` on an arrow.
148	- `kind` required on both payoffs — **the branch already written, held until now**; a price ending's expected `move` as a range (free here; a second paid re-record if added later).
149	- Sentences asking what would *stop* each step and what would *falsify* each ending; a venue contract named where a real one exists.
150	- No search on the first call (7 s to a first tile, measured) and five claims at once; research a base rate only where a reference class can exist, and drop a count under five; a price ending's instrument must appear in its own test.
151	- Three that never touch the fingerprint and can go earlier: a refusal says whether *our rules* or *the answer* caused it; dropped sources and dropped base rates reach the wire; one clarifying clause on PRD anti-pattern 2 (a first draft of a map is not a re-prompt after an edit).
152	
153	**Record on the branch and commit the new recording and cassettes in the same pull request** — "no search on the first call" changes the request body the cassettes match on but *not* the fingerprint, so merging the code first would leave `main` with a green hash over a recording of behaviour the program no longer has.
154	
155	**The existing `hormuz.jsonl` is valid against `main`** (fingerprint byte-identical, checked by the red team) **and lands as it is.** The payoff defect is latent — the model filled the field in all eleven trades.
156	
157	**Not planned** (each was in the first draft as "later, gated"; the red team is right that a gate is still a line on the plan): drafting a skeleton in one streamed call — three sessions for speed the recorded demo does not need; an ensemble for numbers — FR-8 and record 0015 forbid it in so many words, and the one condition that reopens it is the pastcast, which is cut. Both go on the *what I would do next* page. **Kept untouched:** three silent retries; one walk-driver; every refusal an event; provenance decided by us.
158	
159	---
160	
161	## 5. The screen
162	
163	`review2`'s interface audit ran an older branch. On `feat/04a-growth` today six of its findings are fixed (one scrolling panel with measured edge marks; `App.tsx` 1 074 on `main` → 483; the view framed to the stage; a memoised engine state; an error boundary; a light theme). **Still true and demo-deciding: the brief's core interaction has no mouse route** — the six operations open from `e` or the palette only. A **polish pull request** (one session, browser only, after growth lands) carries that button and eight small things a reviewer meets in the first two minutes; its end-to-end check is *geometric* — every control inside the panel's box, at the three window sizes the walk is judged at — never a pixel baseline.
164	
165	Rejected with reasons: a probability slider (every edit appends to an audit trail with no undo — scrubbing writes thirty edits, or opens a second unaudited path; *Change this push* already is the honest version); *Release* / undo-an-edit (in no brief clause, requirement or invariant, and it is a domain, wire and generated-types change, not a button); small multiples; merging the PRD and `ARCHITECTURE.md` (merging does not fix drift — a 40-line test of its **built**/**planned** markers does); a reducer for `MapScreen`.
166	
167	---
168	
169	## 6. Documents and process — targeted, not a freeze
170	
171	- **One owning place for the worked example's numbers.** `make numbers` runs the engine on Hormuz and writes one committed file, inputs and computed numbers labelled apart; the build regenerates it and fails on a difference — the `types-fresh` pattern, already trusted. Chapters may quote and link. When the engine flips, *the diff of that one file is the complete statement of every number that moved.* A lint (a decimal in prose must appear in that file or on a short allow-list) arrives with the engine stack's sweep. Today a documents agent counted about 90 engine-computed numbers across 13 files, and the README's `curl` example prints 16 digits a reader will not get.
172	- **Local cuts to the spec, none a freeze** (craft analyst §3, about 17% by its count): cite the visual checklist by stable name (35 citations by line number today; it has thirteen lines and `ARCHITECTURE.md` says twelve); fold answered open questions into the chapter that owns them; move dated history out of behaviour sections into the records; **change one line of the chapter template** — a *Data model* section gives the shape and names the module, not the class body (those sections run to about 35 000 words, 50–79% identical to the code); one owner per repeated rule. Each rides in the pull request that touches the chapter; none is a sweep of its own.
173	- **A caution the red team earned:** a documents agent reported about twenty workbench passages still saying "there is no engine"; the red team found one such passage — the rest are live, correct vocabulary for an absence (`no engine yet`). **Check each before editing; do not sweep.**
174	- **One record for what version one does not build.** FR-17, FR-18, FR-20, part of FR-24, FR-29, FR-30 and INV-10 are cut here; the definition of done requires every decision to have an accepted record. One short record lists them with a sentence each. **FR-31 (P0: sessions persist to one SQLite file, addressable by URL) is scheduled nowhere and cut nowhere** — it is on Kent's list with a recommendation.
175	- **Process (proposed amendment to record 0009 — Kent's):** a stack is at most **two** deep. Kept: Conventional Commits, branch names, the three headings, squash-merge, always green, and **a read-only reviewer before every pull request** (it found a must-fix on every branch this stack — and on this page). The rule the evidence supports for agents is not a head-count: **one agent per file-owning area; never two agents writing prose about one subject.** Whole suites and browser runs go through one queue (`plans/scripts/heavy.sh`); only the coordinator runs playwright, repeat bars, or anything paid.
176	
177	---
178	
179	## 7. What is not being done, and why
180	
181	| Cut | Why |
182	|---|---|
183	| The path product | Not a probability of anything when claims share causes |
184	| `refine` and INV-10; feedback-loop unrolling; the random-simulation probe | Nothing in the brief asks; research projects over an exact core. INV-10 is met by a named refusal, and the definition of done says so |
185	| The pastcast | Needs evidence frozen before each event, which the pipeline does not have; one resolved event is not a track record. One honest sentence on the *what I would do next* page |
186	| A one-call skeleton; an ensemble for numbers | Speed the recorded demo does not need; forbidden by FR-8 and record 0015, whose only reopening condition is the pastcast |
187	| Expected shortfall, drawdown, ruin, automatic sizing | Need a capital base and a portfolio; theatre without them |
188	| A price-valued fifth kind of claim; two-sided payoffs | A position already holds those numbers; the loss leg is the stop |
189	| Exact inference over event times as the default; full tables per parent combination; enumeration | Measured too slow, or 2^k numbers a model states incoherently |
190	| *Release* / undo-an-edit; a probability slider; small multiples | No clause asks; a domain change dressed as a button; an unaudited edit path; a dashboard |
191	| Freezing `spec/`; merging PRD and `ARCHITECTURE.md`; moving formatting out of `domain/`; splitting `propagation.py` | Kent's correction; or the cost does not clear the bar |
192	| Screenshot baselines; a wall-clock gate in the build | Two flake generators |
193	
194	**Not cut, and the red team is right to insist:** the other three recordings. The brief names four example inputs and FR-3 (P0) puts all four on the launchpad. Kent's instruction stands — *Hormuz only until he explicitly approves* — so it is put to him as a decision: recorded **once**, **after** the freeze, **three at once** in the background, it is about 45 minutes of wall clock and $15, not the two-plus hours of running them back to back.
